content: Why simp tactic is disabled but rfl is not? In Rocq, rfl includes simp.

@Daniil Iaitskov simp/grind are only disabled for easy problems, where we want to check whether the user understands how the proof works. Lean 4's simp searches over different theorems (marked via the @[simp] attribute) about equalities and finds how we can rewrite the current goal in order to prove equality or make current goal more simple. simpl in Rocq is more similar to dsimp only in Lean 4 and it unfolds/reduces only current definitions of goal and tries to bring two sides of equation to the same form(without picking new lemmas from database). In other words, user can prove most of easy problems via simp/grind without understanding how to prove them, while rfl and dsimp are not much automation tactics and they only prove definitional equalities

nnarek said:

found issue with false-implies-anything problem, now it allows to use False.elim

I was able to to solve it by destructing ⊥\bot⊥ hypothesis, does it mean that it implicitly relies on False.elim?
@Daniil Iaitskov when we use exfalso tactic then under the hood it uses False.elim to replace current goal with False. if you destruct h: False via cases h then it is using False.casesOn function.
